From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall:** The package is described as "negotiated" and "agreed", but none of these positions has been agreed. Several are the buyer's fallbacks, which we have no authority to offer. The most serious problems are structural: the limitation clauses sweep in every claim type, and the disclosure and knowledge provisions together would gut the warranties. I only have the Seller's summary, not the full SPA text, so the points below need checking against the actual clauses when we mark up.

## 1. Structural issues (highest priority)

**a) Fraud and misconduct (cl. 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 12.3/13)**
- The Seller applies limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". It also says any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- Read together, these would cap or time-bar fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, and would also override Title, Tax, IP and specific indemnity claims.
- Our position is that fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived by anyone, including at deal-team level.
- The "unless expressly stated" mechanism is a hidden general-regime override. Reverse it so that general limits apply only to General Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own regime.

**b) Fundamental/Title claims**
- The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Our position is a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Title is the thing we are buying, so a 20% cap on it would be unacceptable.

**c) Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2)**
- The Seller discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- We reject whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. We require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties.
- Letter para 11 pushes the burden onto us ("Buyer must evaluate… the current due diligence record"). Reject that framing.
- The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, and we are now in November. Disclosure should not be updatable up to Completion in a way that cures breaches, so check the bring-down mechanics.
- Para 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if it doesn't limit the warranties or indemnities.

**d) Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)**
- This excludes anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge on top of deemed disclosure, and the two compound each other.
- Delete it. If the Seller needs any qualifier, it must be tied to named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

## 2. Commercial terms, and where the Seller sits against the playbook

| Item | Seller | Our position | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | Seller's figure is our conditional fallback. It needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None given. Counter at 6.0m and signal no flexibility. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Five times ours. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Both size and mechanism are wrong. A deductible basket 5x ours means small and medium claims are never recoverable. |
| Claims period | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is also a fallback needing Frost's written approval. None given. |

Don't reveal the existence or content of any fallback. Even a "we'll consider it" response risks being treated as a concession.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

**Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30%)**
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with consent "satisfied on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent.
- Its own Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- We require an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this weight.
- Make it a condition precedent with a long-stop date and a buyer right to terminate. Check the content of the 11.3 conditions, because a consent delivered subject to unmet conditions is not an effective consent.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m outstanding)**
- The Seller proposes a release "following Completion", and para 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. We require a current payout figure, direct repayment out of Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion (check what security exists, including over shares and assets).
- A post-completion release is possible only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so don't offer it.
- Note that change-control clause 8.1 may also be triggered.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)**
- The Seller says it is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow. The funds flow's claim to reflect "agreed price mechanics" is not accurate, because nothing has been agreed.
- These must be a specific funds-flow line item or be seller-funded.
- On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) must be included if triggered. Para 5 is silent on whether they apply, so ask the Seller to confirm with payroll advice. I have not estimated them, and we shouldn't put a number on them until that's confirmed.
- The funds flow must not silently exclude these amounts.

**Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010)**
- The Seller wants the indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. That is too narrow. Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment, so the real exposure is the IP itself.
- Broaden it to cover claims, losses and costs relating to ownership, use or transfer of the Ironquay materials. Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism.
- The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. DD-010 records it as open, but the Seller itself says that is not bank verification. Ask for payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment, and don't assert either that it is owed or that it is paid.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary and that it cannot say whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required.
- "Not expected to be material" is therefore unsupported. Don't accept it, and don't overreact in the other direction either.
- We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The ask is process-based: preserve logs, complete the investigation, give us regular updates and access to findings, and give notice of any change in status. Take privacy advice on notification analysis. Don't attach a price adjustment or loss figure.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000: three at AUD 110,000)**
- The Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs", but its own para 8 doesn't say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Request the contracts and terms and assess them. Make no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction at this stage, and don't accept the Seller's label as settled either.

**Tax and IP**
- The Seller says they are "settled under the general regime". They are open, so reject that. Keep Tax, IP, Title, payment and covenant categories as separate regimes.
- We shouldn't assume unlimited liability or any resolution. Just record that they remain open and outside the general cap and basket pending negotiation.

**Title**
- The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. The register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof, and para 10 of the Disclosure Letter itself says we haven't completed our verification.
- Require independent evidence: ASIC extract, share issue/transfer history and certificates, PPSR and charge searches (cross-check against Riverlark security), constitution and shareholder approvals, and evidence of the Seller's authority and capacity.
- I'm not suggesting title is defective, only that it isn't yet proved.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The disclosure doesn't indicate that consent is needed for the share sale. These are lower priority.
- Confirm by reading the actual clauses, and diarise the DD-007 notification obligation in the Completion checklist.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Respond with a reservation.** Reject the "negotiated/agreed/settled" characterisation. Nothing is agreed, and silence should not be read as acceptance.
2. **Counter on the numbers:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24 months.
3. **Hold the fallbacks.** Don't signal 20% / AUD 4.8m or 18 months. Using either needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none exists. The same applies to a post-completion Riverlark release.
4. **Rebuild the limitations architecture:**
   - A fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
   - A separate Title/capacity regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
   - Delete the "applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise" language.
   - Separate regimes for Tax, IP, payment and covenants.
5. **Disclosure and knowledge:** specific fair disclosure only, delete cl. 8.3, and allow any seller-knowledge qualifier only with named persons and reasonable enquiry.
6. **Closing mechanics:**
   - Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence its conditions are satisfied, as a CP.
   - Riverlark: payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and security releases at Completion.
   - Bonuses: a specific line item or seller-funded, with confirmation of on-costs.
7. **Specific protections:**
   - Ironquay: a broader indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain payment or assignment evidence.
   - DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants, with no assumed breach or figures.
   - Sandbar: assess it, with no Debt reclassification or deduction.
8. **Verification:** obtain independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Confirm the lease and Mossvale readings against the source clauses.
9. **Next steps:** I can draft the mark-up of the key clauses (limitations, disclosure, knowledge, CPs and funds flow) and a short cover response to Seller's counsel. Before we send anything, someone should confirm the actual clause text, since I've worked from the Seller's summary.
